title: Arrays & Hashing

views.title: Arrays & Hashing
views.intro: The core move is turning a nested loop into one pass plus a map: store what you have seen (value, prefix sum, balance) and look up what you need. Most "count subarrays" problems are prefix sum + frequency map.
table: Subarray sum = k, divisible by k, balanced 0/1
Dutch flag, rotate, next permutation, matrices

files.desc: Two sum, subarray sums, product except self, anagram groups, longest consecutive, top K, cyclic sort, Boyer-Moore, Dutch flag, next permutation, rotations, matrix ops, trapping water

pitfalls: Prefix-sum maps must be seeded with {0: 1} (or {0: -1} for earliest index).
Negative mod: normalize with ((x % k) + k) % k.
Longest consecutive: only start counting at sequence heads to stay O(n).

views.title: Arrays: Counting & Chunking
views.intro: Harder array problems are rarely about the array itself: they are counting pairs (merge sort or Fenwick), choosing chunk boundaries (prefix max vs suffix min), or linear-time sorting when keys are bounded.
table: Count pairs i < j with a value relation
Elements appearing more than n/k times

files.desc: Circular max subarray, majority II, find duplicates, count of range sum, reverse pairs, max chunks I and II, longest mountain, best sightseeing pair, bounded-max subarrays, shortest unsorted subarray, max width ramp, two non-overlapping subarrays, radix sort, counting sort, 3-way quicksort

pitfalls: Use long for prefix sums and for 2 * a[j] comparisons in pair counting.
Circular max subarray: if all values are negative the answer is the linear max, not total - min.
Count pairs during merge, before merging, while both halves are still sorted.
